newsitem.title: PERU: Anti-government march turns violent in Peru.
newsitem.headline: Anti-government march turns violent in Peru.

text.p: Protestors clashed with police during a march in downtown Lima on Thursday by several thousand Peruvian workers against increasingly embattled President Alberto Fujimori, witnesses said.
Workers chanting "down with the dictatorship" fought with about 300 police as they burst into the main square opposite Fujimori's Government Palace.
Heavily-armed police cordoned off Government Palace -- where Fujimori was present -- while soldiers stood on the roof watching the estimated 3,000 demonstrators.
A police helicopter flew overhead as workers exchanged blows with police and swarmed over a huge fountain in the centre of the Plaza de Armas opposite the palace.

"It's a good thing there are Peruvians who have the dignity to reject all this ill-treatment from the Fujimori government," said Juan Jose Gorriti, secretary-general of the Peruvian General Workers' Confederation that organised the march.
At least two ministers resigned earlier from Fujimori's cabinet, deepening a crisis that has seen his popularity plunge to the lowest level in seven years.
